addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/Bubka/2FAuth
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: 2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1
7	  port: 8000
8	  vm: m1.small
9	  flavor_id: "2"
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: 2fauth
16	quirks:
17	  - "PIN 2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1, AND NOTE THE TAG STRING DIFFERS FROM THE RELEASE. Docker Hub publishes 8.0.1, 8.0, 8 and a rolling tag; the GitHub release for the same build is v8.0.1, with a leading v. Copying the release name into the compose gives you a pull failure that reads like a network problem. Confirmed against the Docker Hub tag list on 2026-08-17. Never use a rolling tag for a credential store: the entrypoint migrates the schema when the image's commit differs from the marker file, so an unpinned redeploy migrates the vault whenever upstream ships."
18	  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE FIRST PERSON TO SUBMIT THE SIGN-UP FORM, AND THERE IS NO WAY TO CLOSE THAT AT DEPLOY TIME. app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.php promotes the new account to administrator when User::count() == 1, and registration is open because config/2fauth.php seeds disableRegistration = false. That setting lives in the database, not the environment, so there is no variable you can pass to deploy_compose that closes the window. It closes when YOU register. Do it as the first action after the container answers, before the URL goes anywhere, then turn Disable registration ON in Settings, then run the verification script in this file. Never hand over a 2FAuth URL that nobody has claimed: the person who claims it can read every code you later store."
19	  - "⛔⛔ TURN ON \"Protect sensitive data\" OR THE SEEDS SIT IN THE DATABASE IN PLAIN TEXT. config/2fauth.php sets useEncryption = false by default, and app/Models/Traits/CanEncryptField.php only reaches for Laravel's Crypt when that setting is true. Everything else about the deploy can be perfect and the twofaccounts table will still hold every TOTP seed, account name and service name in the clear, readable by anyone who reaches the managed database or a backup of it. Turn it on in the admin settings immediately after you claim the account and BEFORE importing anything real."
20	  - "⛔⛔ APP_KEY IS THE SHARPEST SECRET IN THIS WHOLE LIBRARY, AND IT FAILS QUIETLY. Once encryption is on, APP_KEY decrypts every stored seed. Generate one 32-byte value, keep it, and pass the SAME value on every redeploy. Get it wrong and nothing errors: CanEncryptField::decryptOrReturn catches the exception and returns the translated 'indecipherable' placeholder, so you get a healthy app, a full-looking list of accounts, and not one working code. Losing this key destroys every two-factor account in the vault, which is worse than losing the database, because the user may no longer be able to sign in to the services those codes protect. If you ever must rotate it, put the OLD value in APP_PREVIOUS_KEYS first (.env.example:38-45 documents exactly this) and let the app re-encrypt. ⚠️ An empty APP_KEY does not stop the container either: docker/entrypoint.sh prints a warning line and carries on."
21	  - "⛔⛔ THE /2fauth VOLUME IS NOT OPTIONAL AND LOSING IT WIPES THE MANAGED DATABASE. This is the trap that a managed database makes WORSE rather than better. docker/entrypoint.sh checks for the marker file /2fauth/installed: if it is missing it runs php artisan migrate:fresh --force, which DROPS EVERY TABLE and recreates them empty. The marker lives on the app VM's volume; the accounts live in the managed Postgres. So a fresh app VM pointed at an existing 2FAuth database boots, sees no marker, drops the vault, and comes up perfectly healthy and completely empty. Mount a volume on /2fauth and keep it. If the volume is ever lost, DO NOT boot the image against the surviving database until you have restored it; the marker alone is not enough, because /2fauth also holds the Passport keys and the storage tree. The real backup is the account export from the 2FAuth UI, and it is worth taking before any redeploy."
22	  - "USE A NAMED DOCKER VOLUME FOR /2fauth, NOT A BIND MOUNT. The Dockerfile runs the app as UID 1000 and creates /2fauth chmod 700 owned by 1000:1000. A bind mount from a host directory arrives owned by root and the container, which has no root, cannot write to it; upstream's own compose uses ./2fauth and quietly assumes you fixed that. A named volume inherits the image's ownership on first use and just works."
23	  - "⛔ DATABASE: THE IMAGE SHIPS WITH SQLITE ALREADY CHOSEN. This is not a variable you forget, it is a default you must actively override: the Dockerfile bakes DB_CONNECTION=sqlite and DB_DATABASE=/srv/database/database.sqlite into the image, and the entrypoint symlinks that path to /2fauth/database.sqlite. Set DB_CONNECTION=pgsql and map redu's injected variables yourself, because deploy_compose only appends them to the project .env and never edits your compose: DB_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", DB_PORT=\"${PGPORT}\", DB_DATABASE=\"${PGDATABASE}\", DB_USERNAME=\"${PGUSER}\", DB_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". 2FAuth needs exactly ONE database, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule never bites here."
24	  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE PROVES NOTHING. Positive half, which is also what tells you the exec worked at all: sudo docker exec <container> printenv DB_CONNECTION DB_HOST must print pgsql and the private IP of the managed database. Negative half: sudo docker exec <container> ls -l /2fauth must show NO database.sqlite. If the first command errors, the second one's empty output means nothing. The VM runs docker, not podman."
25	  - "SET APP_URL TO THE FULL https HOSTNAME OR WEBAUTHN NEVER WORKS. .env.example is explicit: the variable must match the installation's external address or WebAuthn breaks, because the browser binds a passkey to the origin. Since it has to be known before the container starts, GENERATE THE dname YOURSELF in the full 2fauth-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form and pass it as APP_URL; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. Set TRUSTED_PROXIES=* at the same time (it defaults to null), because redu terminates TLS at its proxy and 2FAuth otherwise records the proxy's address for every login and can misjudge whether the request was secure."
26	  - "PORT 8000, and the health anchor is GET /up. The Dockerfile exposes 8000/tcp and nginx listens there. routes/web.php strips session, CSRF, binding and language middleware off /up, so it answers before anything else is ready, and its body links healthcheck.css, which is a 2FAuth-specific string that does not depend on APP_NAME. Pass 8000 to deploy_compose. There is no HEALTHCHECK in the image."
27	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, ANSWERED PLAINLY. GET /up; GET /manifest.json; GET /api/v1/user/name, a deprecated stub that returns {'deprecation': true} and nothing else; and the landing page, whose inline script carries the real values of disableRegistration, enableSso and useSsoOnly while every other setting is deliberately nulled (SinglePageController.php). No account data, no seeds and no user list are reachable without authentication. The one thing an anonymous visitor CAN do on a fresh instance is claim the administrator account, which is the quirk above."
28	  - "THE ADMIN PASSWORD IS THE ONLY WAY BACK IN BY DEFAULT. Mail is unconfigured out of the box, so the 'lost password' e-mail goes nowhere, and the recovery paths that exist (password reset by e-mail, WebAuthn device recovery) both need working SMTP. Hand the password to the user in the session and tell them to store it somewhere that is NOT this instance. ⚠️ There is a real circularity here worth saying out loud: this app holds the second factor for their other accounts, so locking themselves out of it is expensive. Configure MAIL_* and SITE_OWNER if they want recovery, or add a passkey once they are signed in."
29	  - "USE UPSTREAM'S COMPOSE AS A SHAPE, NOT A FILE. docker/docker-compose.yml is four useful lines: one service, the image, a volume at /2fauth and port 8000. Drop the obsolete version key, drop the env_file indirection that points at settings.env, and write the environment inline so the PG* interpolation is visible, and use a named volume as described above. There are no bundled databases, proxies or sidecars to delete, which is why this is one of the cheapest entries here."
30	  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED, AND DO NOT ADD ONE. docker/entrypoint.sh runs the migrations itself, chooses between migrate and migrate:fresh on the marker file, runs passport:install on a genuinely fresh install, then optimizes and starts supervisord. Adding your own migrate step can only interfere with that decision. QUEUE_DRIVER is sync and CACHE_DRIVER and SESSION_DRIVER are file, so no Redis is needed; sessions land in /2fauth/storage and survive a container restart."
31	  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO FIGURE. It is an alpine image running nginx and php-fpm for one small Laravel app, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this one of the cheapest entries in the library. The one thing that spikes is QR-code decoding: .env.example documents PHP_MEMORY_LIMIT_TEMP_OVERRIDE=512, a temporary 512 MB per-request limit applied so image scanning does not exhaust memory. That fits inside 2 GB for a personal vault; move to m1.medium if a team will be importing at once. Measure it on your run and write the number back rather than repeating this paragraph."
32	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.035/hr, roughly GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 8000. ⚠️ plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large; passing flavor_id '2' explicitly holds m1.small, and the larger floor exists for stacks that BUILD from source, which this does not. Always pass db_flavor_id explicitly or the database VM inherits the app flavor and doubles the bill."
33	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar and curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
34	  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, read from the LICENSE file, and this one has a clause worth a sentence. Section 13 says that if you MODIFY the program and let other people use it over a network, you must offer those users the modified source. Running the published image unmodified for yourself or your team creates no such obligation. It falls on whoever OPERATES the service, which here is the user, not redu, and it is one more reason to deploy the pinned upstream image rather than a fork."
35	  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. APP_KEY, the admin password and the database password all belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that an admin exists, that registration is closed and that encryption is on, never the values. Generate the password alphanumeric so there is nothing to escape in JSON or the shell."
36	  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. ⚠️ The merge does NOT write new quirks: when this file is richer than redu's template it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Anything the run teaches has to be added by hand."
37	  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, AND THAT COMBINATION IS DANGEROUS HERE. delete_deployment removes the app VM and the /2fauth volume with it, while the managed Postgres keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr with every account still in it. Redeploying onto that surviving database with no volume is exactly the migrate:fresh wipe described above. So either delete the database too with delete_database, or restore the volume before the next boot. Say which, plainly, before deleting anything."
38	---
39	
40	# Self-host 2FAuth on redu
41	
42	Your two-factor codes on your own machine: one small container, a managed Postgres, a public HTTPS
43	URL. About GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial, and one of the cheapest entries here.
44	
45	## What this deploys
46	
47	- **2FAuth** from the official Docker Hub image, pinned to `8.0.1`, on one m1.small VM, port 8000.
48	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the accounts.
49	- A named volume on `/2fauth`, which holds the storage tree, the Passport keys and the install
50	  marker. Read the warning below before you treat it as disposable.
51	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
52	
53	## Deploy
54	
55	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
56	directory containing this file:
57	
58	    Read redu.md and deploy 2FAuth on redu.
59	
60	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
61	
62	## Three things, and all three lose data
63	
64	**Claim the account immediately.** The first person to submit the sign-up form becomes the
65	administrator, and there is no environment variable that closes that window before the hostname is
66	live. The setting that disables registration lives in the database and can only be set from inside

103	  "$ADMIN_NAME" "$ADMIN_EMAIL" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" |
104	  curl -sS -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" -X POST "https://$HOST/user" \

file.content:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/Bubka/2FAuth
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: 2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1
  port: 8000
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: 2fauth
quirks:
  - "PIN 2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1, AND NOTE THE TAG STRING DIFFERS FROM THE RELEASE. Docker Hub publishes 8.0.1, 8.0, 8 and a rolling tag; the GitHub release for the same build is v8.0.1, with a leading v. Copying the release name into the compose gives you a pull failure that reads like a network problem. Confirmed against the Docker Hub tag list on 2026-08-17. Never use a rolling tag for a credential store: the entrypoint migrates the schema when the image's commit differs from the marker file, so an unpinned redeploy migrates the vault whenever upstream ships."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE FIRST PERSON TO SUBMIT THE SIGN-UP FORM, AND THERE IS NO WAY TO CLOSE THAT AT DEPLOY TIME. app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.php promotes the new account to administrator when User::count() == 1, and registration is open because config/2fauth.php seeds disableRegistration = false. That setting lives in the database, not the environment, so there is no variable you can pass to deploy_compose that closes the window. It closes when YOU register. Do it as the first action after the container answers, before the URL goes anywhere, then turn Disable registration ON in Settings, then run the verification script in this file. Never hand over a 2FAuth URL that nobody has claimed: the person who claims it can read every code you later store."
  - "⛔⛔ TURN ON \"Protect sensitive data\" OR THE SEEDS SIT IN THE DATABASE IN PLAIN TEXT. config/2fauth.php sets useEncryption = false by default, and app/Models/Traits/CanEncryptField.php only reaches for Laravel's Crypt when that setting is true. Everything else about the deploy can be perfect and the twofaccounts table will still hold every TOTP seed, account name and service name in the clear, readable by anyone who reaches the managed database or a backup of it. Turn it on in the admin settings immediately after you claim the account and BEFORE importing anything real."
  - "⛔⛔ APP_KEY IS THE SHARPEST SECRET IN THIS WHOLE LIBRARY, AND IT FAILS QUIETLY. Once encryption is on, APP_KEY decrypts every stored seed. Generate one 32-byte value, keep it, and pass the SAME value on every redeploy. Get it wrong and nothing errors: CanEncryptField::decryptOrReturn catches the exception and returns the translated 'indecipherable' placeholder, so you get a healthy app, a full-looking list of accounts, and not one working code. Losing this key destroys every two-factor account in the vault, which is worse than losing the database, because the user may no longer be able to sign in to the services those codes protect. If you ever must rotate it, put the OLD value in APP_PREVIOUS_KEYS first (.env.example:38-45 documents exactly this) and let the app re-encrypt. ⚠️ An empty APP_KEY does not stop the container either: docker/entrypoint.sh prints a warning line and carries on."
  - "⛔⛔ THE /2fauth VOLUME IS NOT OPTIONAL AND LOSING IT WIPES THE MANAGED DATABASE. This is the trap that a managed database makes WORSE rather than better. docker/entrypoint.sh checks for the marker file /2fauth/installed: if it is missing it runs php artisan migrate:fresh --force, which DROPS EVERY TABLE and recreates them empty. The marker lives on the app VM's volume; the accounts live in the managed Postgres. So a fresh app VM pointed at an existing 2FAuth database boots, sees no marker, drops the vault, and comes up perfectly healthy and completely empty. Mount a volume on /2fauth and keep it. If the volume is ever lost, DO NOT boot the image against the surviving database until you have restored it; the marker alone is not enough, because /2fauth also holds the Passport keys and the storage tree. The real backup is the account export from the 2FAuth UI, and it is worth taking before any redeploy."
  - "USE A NAMED DOCKER VOLUME FOR /2fauth, NOT A BIND MOUNT. The Dockerfile runs the app as UID 1000 and creates /2fauth chmod 700 owned by 1000:1000. A bind mount from a host directory arrives owned by root and the container, which has no root, cannot write to it; upstream's own compose uses ./2fauth and quietly assumes you fixed that. A named volume inherits the image's ownership on first use and just works."
  - "⛔ DATABASE: THE IMAGE SHIPS WITH SQLITE ALREADY CHOSEN. This is not a variable you forget, it is a default you must actively override: the Dockerfile bakes DB_CONNECTION=sqlite and DB_DATABASE=/srv/database/database.sqlite into the image, and the entrypoint symlinks that path to /2fauth/database.sqlite. Set DB_CONNECTION=pgsql and map redu's injected variables yourself, because deploy_compose only appends them to the project .env and never edits your compose: DB_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", DB_PORT=\"${PGPORT}\", DB_DATABASE=\"${PGDATABASE}\", DB_USERNAME=\"${PGUSER}\", DB_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". 2FAuth needs exactly ONE database, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule never bites here."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE PROVES NOTHING. Positive half, which is also what tells you the exec worked at all: sudo docker exec <container> printenv DB_CONNECTION DB_HOST must print pgsql and the private IP of the managed database. Negative half: sudo docker exec <container> ls -l /2fauth must show NO database.sqlite. If the first command errors, the second one's empty output means nothing. The VM runs docker, not podman."
  - "SET APP_URL TO THE FULL https HOSTNAME OR WEBAUTHN NEVER WORKS. .env.example is explicit: the variable must match the installation's external address or WebAuthn breaks, because the browser binds a passkey to the origin. Since it has to be known before the container starts, GENERATE THE dname YOURSELF in the full 2fauth-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form and pass it as APP_URL; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. Set TRUSTED_PROXIES=* at the same time (it defaults to null), because redu terminates TLS at its proxy and 2FAuth otherwise records the proxy's address for every login and can misjudge whether the request was secure."
  - "PORT 8000, and the health anchor is GET /up. The Dockerfile exposes 8000/tcp and nginx listens there. routes/web.php strips session, CSRF, binding and language middleware off /up, so it answers before anything else is ready, and its body links healthcheck.css, which is a 2FAuth-specific string that does not depend on APP_NAME. Pass 8000 to deploy_compose. There is no HEALTHCHECK in the image."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, ANSWERED PLAINLY. GET /up; GET /manifest.json; GET /api/v1/user/name, a deprecated stub that returns {'deprecation': true} and nothing else; and the landing page, whose inline script carries the real values of disableRegistration, enableSso and useSsoOnly while every other setting is deliberately nulled (SinglePageController.php). No account data, no seeds and no user list are reachable without authentication. The one thing an anonymous visitor CAN do on a fresh instance is claim the administrator account, which is the quirk above."
  - "THE ADMIN PASSWORD IS THE ONLY WAY BACK IN BY DEFAULT. Mail is unconfigured out of the box, so the 'lost password' e-mail goes nowhere, and the recovery paths that exist (password reset by e-mail, WebAuthn device recovery) both need working SMTP. Hand the password to the user in the session and tell them to store it somewhere that is NOT this instance. ⚠️ There is a real circularity here worth saying out loud: this app holds the second factor for their other accounts, so locking themselves out of it is expensive. Configure MAIL_* and SITE_OWNER if they want recovery, or add a passkey once they are signed in."
  - "USE UPSTREAM'S COMPOSE AS A SHAPE, NOT A FILE. docker/docker-compose.yml is four useful lines: one service, the image, a volume at /2fauth and port 8000. Drop the obsolete version key, drop the env_file indirection that points at settings.env, and write the environment inline so the PG* interpolation is visible, and use a named volume as described above. There are no bundled databases, proxies or sidecars to delete, which is why this is one of the cheapest entries here."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED, AND DO NOT ADD ONE. docker/entrypoint.sh runs the migrations itself, chooses between migrate and migrate:fresh on the marker file, runs passport:install on a genuinely fresh install, then optimizes and starts supervisord. Adding your own migrate step can only interfere with that decision. QUEUE_DRIVER is sync and CACHE_DRIVER and SESSION_DRIVER are file, so no Redis is needed; sessions land in /2fauth/storage and survive a container restart."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO FIGURE. It is an alpine image running nginx and php-fpm for one small Laravel app, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this one of the cheapest entries in the library. The one thing that spikes is QR-code decoding: .env.example documents PHP_MEMORY_LIMIT_TEMP_OVERRIDE=512, a temporary 512 MB per-request limit applied so image scanning does not exhaust memory. That fits inside 2 GB for a personal vault; move to m1.medium if a team will be importing at once. Measure it on your run and write the number back rather than repeating this paragraph."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.035/hr, roughly GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 8000. ⚠️ plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large; passing flavor_id '2' explicitly holds m1.small, and the larger floor exists for stacks that BUILD from source, which this does not. Always pass db_flavor_id explicitly or the database VM inherits the app flavor and doubles the bill."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar and curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, read from the LICENSE file, and this one has a clause worth a sentence. Section 13 says that if you MODIFY the program and let other people use it over a network, you must offer those users the modified source. Running the published image unmodified for yourself or your team creates no such obligation. It falls on whoever OPERATES the service, which here is the user, not redu, and it is one more reason to deploy the pinned upstream image rather than a fork."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. APP_KEY, the admin password and the database password all belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that an admin exists, that registration is closed and that encryption is on, never the values. Generate the password alphanumeric so there is nothing to escape in JSON or the shell."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. ⚠️ The merge does NOT write new quirks: when this file is richer than redu's template it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Anything the run teaches has to be added by hand."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, AND THAT COMBINATION IS DANGEROUS HERE. delete_deployment removes the app VM and the /2fauth volume with it, while the managed Postgres keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr with every account still in it. Redeploying onto that surviving database with no volume is exactly the migrate:fresh wipe described above. So either delete the database too with delete_database, or restore the volume before the next boot. Say which, plainly, before deleting anything."
---

# Self-host 2FAuth on redu

Your two-factor codes on your own machine: one small container, a managed Postgres, a public HTTPS
URL. About GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial, and one of the cheapest entries here.

## What this deploys

- **2FAuth** from the official Docker Hub image, pinned to `8.0.1`, on one m1.small VM, port 8000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the accounts.
- A named volume on `/2fauth`, which holds the storage tree, the Passport keys and the install
  marker. Read the warning below before you treat it as disposable.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy 2FAuth on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Three things, and all three lose data

**Claim the account immediately.** The first person to submit the sign-up form becomes the
administrator, and there is no environment variable that closes that window before the hostname is
live. The setting that disables registration lives in the database and can only be set from inside
the app. So the window closes when you register, and not a moment earlier.

**Turn on encryption before you store anything.** 2FAuth ships with `useEncryption` off, which
means the seeds sit in the database in plain text. Turn on "Protect sensitive data" in the admin
settings first, then import.

**Keep `APP_KEY` and keep the `/2fauth` volume.** The key decrypts every seed, and a wrong one
does not error: the app shows a full list of accounts and not one working code. The volume holds
the install marker, and without it the container drops every table in your managed database and
comes up healthy and empty.

## Claim the administrator account

Run this the moment the container answers. Generate the password alphanumeric, at least eight
characters, and never write it into this file.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:?usage: claim.sh <2fauth-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud>}"
: "${ADMIN_NAME:?set ADMIN_NAME}"
: "${ADMIN_EMAIL:?set ADMIN_EMAIL}"
: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:[REDACTED:value] ADMIN_PASSWORD, at least 8 characters}"

JAR=$(mktemp)
OUT=$(mktemp)

# The registration endpoint is a session route, so it needs a CSRF token from the same session.
TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:ce5757dd» -sS -c "$JAR" "https://$HOST/refresh-csrf")
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no CSRF token returned, the app is probably still starting. Re-run."
  exit 3
fi

# printf is a shell builtin, so the password never appears in ps, and the body goes on stdin.
code=$(printf '{"name":"%s","email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]","password_confirmation":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
  "$ADMIN_NAME" "$ADMIN_EMAIL" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" |
  curl -sS -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" -X POST "https://$HOST/user" \
    -H "X-CSRF-TOKEN: [REDACTED:value]" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'Accept: application/json' \
    --data-binary @- -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}')

if [ "$code" != "201" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: registration answered $code, not 201. Body:"
  cat "$OUT"
  echo
  echo "Register in a browser NOW instead, and do not leave this instance unclaimed."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: administrator account created. Now sign in and, in Settings:"
echo "  1. turn ON  'Protect sensitive data'   (this is what encrypts the seeds)"
echo "  2. turn ON  'Disable registration'     (this is what closes the door)"
echo "Then run verify.sh."
```

## Then prove it, from outside

This refuses to guess. It establishes that it is talking to 2FAuth before it believes anything, and
exits 3 rather than passing when it cannot tell.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
HOST="${1:?usage: verify.sh <2fauth-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud>}"
body=$(mktemp)

# (1) require 200. redu's proxy answers 502 for the first couple of minutes while the container
# starts, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" assertion below.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/up")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run in a minute."
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /up answered $code, not 200. Nothing below can be trusted."
  exit 3
fi

# (2) require something app-specific. healthcheck.css is 2FAuth's own and, unlike the heading,
# does not change when APP_NAME does.
if ! grep -q 'healthcheck.css' "$body"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /up answered 200 but the body is not 2FAuth's health page."
  exit 3
fi
echo "OK: talking to 2FAuth"

# (3) positive control for step 4: the landing page really does carry the settings blob, so an
# assertion about its contents can mean something. Without this, a changed template reads as a pass.
land=$(mktemp)
curl -sS -o "$land" "https://$HOST/"
if ! grep -q 'var appSettings = {' "$land"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the landing page has no appSettings block. The template moved; check by hand."
  exit 3
fi
echo "OK: settings block present"

# (4) the assertion. This flag is on the enforcement path: RegisterController returns 403 when it
# is true, for the first account as well as later ones.
if ! grep -q '"disableRegistration":true' "$land"; then
  echo "FAIL: registration is still OPEN. Anyone can create an account on this instance."
  echo "      If nobody has registered yet, the NEXT visitor becomes the administrator."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: registration is closed"
echo
echo "Still to check by hand, because no anonymous request can see it: that 'Protect sensitive"
echo "data' is ON in Settings. The seeds are stored in clear text until it is."
```

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/Bubka/2FAuth
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: 2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1
  port: 8000
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: 2fauth
quirks:
  - "PIN 2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1, AND NOTE THE TAG STRING DIFFERS FROM THE RELEASE. Docker Hub publishes 8.0.1, 8.0, 8 and a rolling tag; the GitHub release for the same build is v8.0.1, with a leading v. Copying the release name into the compose gives you a pull failure that reads like a network problem. Confirmed against the Docker Hub tag list on 2026-08-17. Never use a rolling tag for a credential store: the entrypoint migrates the schema when the image's commit differs from the marker file, so an unpinned redeploy migrates the vault whenever upstream ships."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE FIRST PERSON TO SUBMIT THE SIGN-UP FORM, AND THERE IS NO WAY TO CLOSE THAT AT DEPLOY TIME. app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.php promotes the new account to administrator when User::count() == 1, and registration is open because config/2fauth.php seeds disableRegistration = false. That setting lives in the database, not the environment, so there is no variable you can pass to deploy_compose that closes the window. It closes when YOU register. Do it as the first action after the container answers, before the URL goes anywhere, then turn Disable registration ON in Settings, then run the verification script in this file. Never hand over a 2FAuth URL that nobody has claimed: the person who claims it can read every code you later store."
  - "⛔⛔ TURN ON \"Protect sensitive data\" OR THE SEEDS SIT IN THE DATABASE IN PLAIN TEXT. config/2fauth.php sets useEncryption = false by default, and app/Models/Traits/CanEncryptField.php only reaches for Laravel's Crypt when that setting is true. Everything else about the deploy can be perfect and the twofaccounts table will still hold every TOTP seed, account name and service name in the clear, readable by anyone who reaches the managed database or a backup of it. Turn it on in the admin settings immediately after you claim the account and BEFORE importing anything real."
  - "⛔⛔ APP_KEY IS THE SHARPEST SECRET IN THIS WHOLE LIBRARY, AND IT FAILS QUIETLY. Once encryption is on, APP_KEY decrypts every stored seed. Generate one 32-byte value, keep it, and pass the SAME value on every redeploy. Get it wrong and nothing errors: CanEncryptField::decryptOrReturn catches the exception and returns the translated 'indecipherable' placeholder, so you get a healthy app, a full-looking list of accounts, and not one working code. Losing this key destroys every two-factor account in the vault, which is worse than losing the database, because the user may no longer be able to sign in to the services those codes protect. If you ever must rotate it, put the OLD value in APP_PREVIOUS_KEYS first (.env.example:38-45 documents exactly this) and let the app re-encrypt. ⚠️ An empty APP_KEY does not stop the container either: docker/entrypoint.sh prints a warning line and carries on."
  - "⛔⛔ THE /2fauth VOLUME IS NOT OPTIONAL AND LOSING IT WIPES THE MANAGED DATABASE. This is the trap that a managed database makes WORSE rather than better. docker/entrypoint.sh checks for the marker file /2fauth/installed: if it is missing it runs php artisan migrate:fresh --force, which DROPS EVERY TABLE and recreates them empty. The marker lives on the app VM's volume; the accounts live in the managed Postgres. So a fresh app VM pointed at an existing 2FAuth database boots, sees no marker, drops the vault, and comes up perfectly healthy and completely empty. Mount a volume on /2fauth and keep it. If the volume is ever lost, DO NOT boot the image against the surviving database until you have restored it; the marker alone is not enough, because /2fauth also holds the Passport keys and the storage tree. The real backup is the account export from the 2FAuth UI, and it is worth taking before any redeploy."
  - "USE A NAMED DOCKER VOLUME FOR /2fauth, NOT A BIND MOUNT. The Dockerfile runs the app as UID 1000 and creates /2fauth chmod 700 owned by 1000:1000. A bind mount from a host directory arrives owned by root and the container, which has no root, cannot write to it; upstream's own compose uses ./2fauth and quietly assumes you fixed that. A named volume inherits the image's ownership on first use and just works."
  - "⛔ DATABASE: THE IMAGE SHIPS WITH SQLITE ALREADY CHOSEN. This is not a variable you forget, it is a default you must actively override: the Dockerfile bakes DB_CONNECTION=sqlite and DB_DATABASE=/srv/database/database.sqlite into the image, and the entrypoint symlinks that path to /2fauth/database.sqlite. Set DB_CONNECTION=pgsql and map redu's injected variables yourself, because deploy_compose only appends them to the project .env and never edits your compose: DB_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", DB_PORT=\"${PGPORT}\", DB_DATABASE=\"${PGDATABASE}\", DB_USERNAME=\"${PGUSER}\", DB_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". 2FAuth needs exactly ONE database, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule never bites here."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE PROVES NOTHING. Positive half, which is also what tells you the exec worked at all: sudo docker exec <container> printenv DB_CONNECTION DB_HOST must print pgsql and the private IP of the managed database. Negative half: sudo docker exec <container> ls -l /2fauth must show NO database.sqlite. If the first command errors, the second one's empty output means nothing. The VM runs docker, not podman."
  - "SET APP_URL TO THE FULL https HOSTNAME OR WEBAUTHN NEVER WORKS. .env.example is explicit: the variable must match the installation's external address or WebAuthn breaks, because the browser binds a passkey to the origin. Since it has to be known before the container starts, GENERATE THE dname YOURSELF in the full 2fauth-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form and pass it as APP_URL; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. Set TRUSTED_PROXIES=* at the same time (it defaults to null), because redu terminates TLS at its proxy and 2FAuth otherwise records the proxy's address for every login and can misjudge whether the request was secure."
  - "PORT 8000, and the health anchor is GET /up. The Dockerfile exposes 8000/tcp and nginx listens there. routes/web.php strips session, CSRF, binding and language middleware off /up, so it answers before anything else is ready, and its body links healthcheck.css, which is a 2FAuth-specific string that does not depend on APP_NAME. Pass 8000 to deploy_compose. There is no HEALTHCHECK in the image."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, ANSWERED PLAINLY. GET /up; GET /manifest.json; GET /api/v1/user/name, a deprecated stub that returns {'deprecation': true} and nothing else; and the landing page, whose inline script carries the real values of disableRegistration, enableSso and useSsoOnly while every other setting is deliberately nulled (SinglePageController.php). No account data, no seeds and no user list are reachable without authentication. The one thing an anonymous visitor CAN do on a fresh instance is claim the administrator account, which is the quirk above."
  - "THE ADMIN PASSWORD IS THE ONLY WAY BACK IN BY DEFAULT. Mail is unconfigured out of the box, so the 'lost password' e-mail goes nowhere, and the recovery paths that exist (password reset by e-mail, WebAuthn device recovery) both need working SMTP. Hand the password to the user in the session and tell them to store it somewhere that is NOT this instance. ⚠️ There is a real circularity here worth saying out loud: this app holds the second factor for their other accounts, so locking themselves out of it is expensive. Configure MAIL_* and SITE_OWNER if they want recovery, or add a passkey once they are signed in."
  - "USE UPSTREAM'S COMPOSE AS A SHAPE, NOT A FILE. docker/docker-compose.yml is four useful lines: one service, the image, a volume at /2fauth and port 8000. Drop the obsolete version key, drop the env_file indirection that points at settings.env, and write the environment inline so the PG* interpolation is visible, and use a named volume as described above. There are no bundled databases, proxies or sidecars to delete, which is why this is one of the cheapest entries here."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED, AND DO NOT ADD ONE. docker/entrypoint.sh runs the migrations itself, chooses between migrate and migrate:fresh on the marker file, runs passport:install on a genuinely fresh install, then optimizes and starts supervisord. Adding your own migrate step can only interfere with that decision. QUEUE_DRIVER is sync and CACHE_DRIVER and SESSION_DRIVER are file, so no Redis is needed; sessions land in /2fauth/storage and survive a container restart."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO FIGURE. It is an alpine image running nginx and php-fpm for one small Laravel app, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this one of the cheapest entries in the library. The one thing that spikes is QR-code decoding: .env.example documents PHP_MEMORY_LIMIT_TEMP_OVERRIDE=512, a temporary 512 MB per-request limit applied so image scanning does not exhaust memory. That fits inside 2 GB for a personal vault; move to m1.medium if a team will be importing at once. Measure it on your run and write the number back rather than repeating this paragraph."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.035/hr, roughly GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 8000. ⚠️ plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large; passing flavor_id '2' explicitly holds m1.small, and the larger floor exists for stacks that BUILD from source, which this does not. Always pass db_flavor_id explicitly or the database VM inherits the app flavor and doubles the bill."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar and curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, read from the LICENSE file, and this one has a clause worth a sentence. Section 13 says that if you MODIFY the program and let other people use it over a network, you must offer those users the modified source. Running the published image unmodified for yourself or your team creates no such obligation. It falls on whoever OPERATES the service, which here is the user, not redu, and it is one more reason to deploy the pinned upstream image rather than a fork."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. APP_KEY, the admin password and the database password all belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that an admin exists, that registration is closed and that encryption is on, never the values. Generate the password alphanumeric so there is nothing to escape in JSON or the shell."

Anything the run teaches has to be added by hand."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, AND THAT COMBINATION IS DANGEROUS HERE. delete_deployment removes the app VM and the /2fauth volume with it, while the managed Postgres keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr with every account still in it. Redeploying onto that surviving database with no volume is exactly the migrate:fresh wipe described above. So either delete the database too with delete_database, or restore the volume before the next boot. Say which, plainly, before deleting anything."

# Self-host 2FAuth on redu

Your two-factor codes on your own machine: one small container, a managed Postgres, a public HTTPS
URL. About GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial, and one of the cheapest entries here.

## What this deploys

- **2FAuth** from the official Docker Hub image, pinned to `8.0.1`, on one m1.small VM, port 8000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the accounts.
- A named volume on `/2fauth`, which holds the storage tree, the Passport keys and the install
  marker. Read the warning below before you treat it as disposable.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy 2FAuth on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Three things, and all three lose data

**Claim the account immediately.** The first person to submit the sign-up form becomes the
administrator, and there is no environment variable that closes that window before the hostname is
live. The setting that disables registration lives in the database and can only be set from inside
the app. So the window closes when you register, and not a moment earlier.

**Turn on encryption before you store anything.** 2FAuth ships with `useEncryption` off, which
means the seeds sit in the database in plain text. Turn on "Protect sensitive data" in the admin
settings first, then import.

**Keep `APP_KEY` and keep the `/2fauth` volume.** The key decrypts every seed, and a wrong one
does not error: the app shows a full list of accounts and not one working code. The volume holds
the install marker, and without it the container drops every table in your managed database and
comes up healthy and empty.

## Claim the administrator account

Run this the moment the container answers. Generate the password alphanumeric, at least eight
characters, and never write it into this file.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:?usage: claim.sh <2fauth-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud>}"
: "${ADMIN_NAME:?set ADMIN_NAME}"
: "${ADMIN_EMAIL:?set ADMIN_EMAIL}"
: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:[REDACTED:value] ADMIN_PASSWORD, at least 8 characters}"

JAR=$(mktemp)
OUT=$(mktemp)

# The registration endpoint is a session route, so it needs a CSRF token from the same session.
TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:ce5757dd» -sS -c "$JAR" "https://$HOST/refresh-csrf")
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no CSRF token returned, the app is probably still starting. Re-run."
  exit 3
fi

# printf is a shell builtin, so the password never appears in ps, and the body goes on stdin.
code=$(printf '{"name":"%s","email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]","password_confirmation":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
  "$ADMIN_NAME" "$ADMIN_EMAIL" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" |
  curl -sS -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" -X POST "https://$HOST/user" \
    -H "X-CSRF-TOKEN: [REDACTED:value]" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'Accept: application/json' \
    --data-binary @- -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}')

if [ "$code" != "201" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: registration answered $code, not 201. Body:"
  cat "$OUT"
  echo
  echo "Register in a browser NOW instead, and do not leave this instance unclaimed."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: administrator account created. Now sign in and, in Settings:"
echo "  1. turn ON  'Protect sensitive data'   (this is what encrypts the seeds)"
echo "  2. turn ON  'Disable registration'     (this is what closes the door)"
echo "Then run verify.sh."
```

## Then prove it, from outside

This refuses to guess. It establishes that it is talking to 2FAuth before it believes anything, and
exits 3 rather than passing when it cannot tell.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
HOST="${1:?usage: verify.sh <2fauth-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud>}"
body=$(mktemp)

# (1) require 200. redu's proxy answers 502 for the first couple of minutes while the container
# starts, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" assertion below.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/up")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run in a minute."
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /up answered $code, not 200. Nothing below can be trusted."
  exit 3
fi

# (2) require something app-specific. healthcheck.css is 2FAuth's own and, unlike the heading,
# does not change when APP_NAME does.
if ! grep -q 'healthcheck.css' "$body"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /up answered 200 but the body is not 2FAuth's health page."
  exit 3
fi
echo "OK: talking to 2FAuth"

# (3) positive control for step 4: the landing page really does carry the settings blob, so an
# assertion about its contents can mean something. Without this, a changed template reads as a pass.
land=$(mktemp)
curl -sS -o "$land" "https://$HOST/"
if ! grep -q 'var appSettings = {' "$land"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the landing page has no appSettings block. The template moved; check by hand."
  exit 3
fi
echo "OK: settings block present"

# (4) the assertion. This flag is on the enforcement path: RegisterController returns 403 when it
# is true, for the first account as well as later ones.
if ! grep -q '"disableRegistration":true' "$land"; then
  echo "FAIL: registration is still OPEN. Anyone can create an account on this instance."
  echo "      If nobody has registered yet, the NEXT visitor becomes the administrator."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: registration is closed"
echo
echo "Still to check by hand, because no anonymous request can see it: that 'Protect sensitive"
echo "data' is ON in Settings. The seeds are stored in clear text until it is."
```

Plan is written to `redu-deploy-plan.md`. Here it is:

**2FAuth on redu** — prebuilt image `2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1`, nothing gets built.

| Resource | Rate | Monthly (730h) |
|---|---|---|
| App VM — m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) | GBP 0.0174/hr | GBP 12.70 |
| Managed Postgres — m1.small, own private VM | GBP 0.0174/hr | GBP 12.70 |
| **Total** | **GBP 0.0348/hr** | **GBP 25.40** |

Billed hourly, delete anytime. Inside the no-card free trial.

- URL fixed up front: **https://2fauth-yeowtiia.redu.cloud** — it has to be known before the container starts, because `APP_URL` must match the external origin or WebAuthn passkeys never work.
- Named volume → `/2fauth`. This is load-bearing: the entrypoint runs `migrate:fresh` when the `/2fauth/installed` marker is missing, so a lost volume drops every table in the managed Postgres and comes up healthy and empty.
- `APP_KEY` generated locally and passed via the project `.env`, never into the compose file or redu.md. It decrypts every seed, and a wrong one fails silently.
- No `migrate_command` — the image's entrypoint migrates itself and picks `migrate` vs `migrate:fresh` off that marker.

Two deviations from what `plan_deploy` returned, both deliberate:

1. It sized the app VM at **m1.large — GBP 48.18/mo**. That floor exists for stacks that build from source; this pulls a prebuilt alpine image running nginx + php-fpm. I'm holding m1.small, which is what redu.md records from the last run.
2. It flagged `flavor-differs-from-record` for exactly that reason — answered above.

One thing I need before the container goes live: the moment it answers, **the first person to submit the sign-up form becomes the administrator**, and there is no deploy-time setting that closes that window — the flag lives in the database. So I'll claim the account immediately, then turn on encryption and close registration before the URL goes anywhere.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:?usage: claim.sh <2fauth-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud>}"
: "${ADMIN_NAME:?set ADMIN_NAME}"
: "${ADMIN_EMAIL:?set ADMIN_EMAIL}"
: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:[REDACTED:value] ADMIN_PASSWORD, at least 8 characters}"

JAR=$(mktemp)
OUT=$(mktemp)

# The registration endpoint is a session route, so it needs a CSRF token from the same session.
TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:ce5757dd» -sS -c "$JAR" "https://$HOST/refresh-csrf")
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no CSRF token returned, the app is probably still starting. Re-run."
  exit 3
fi

# printf is a shell builtin, so the password never appears in ps, and the body goes on stdin.
code=$(printf '{"name":"%s","email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]","password_confirmation":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
  "$ADMIN_NAME" "$ADMIN_EMAIL" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" |
  curl -sS -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" -X POST "https://$HOST/user" \
    -H "X-CSRF-TOKEN: [REDACTED:value]" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'Accept: application/json' \
    --data-binary @- -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}')

if [ "$code" != "201" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: registration answered $code, not 201. Body:"
  cat "$OUT"
  echo
  echo "Register in a browser NOW instead, and do not leave this instance unclaimed."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: administrator account created. Now sign in and, in Settings:"
echo "  1. turn ON  'Protect sensitive data'   (this is what encrypts the seeds)"
echo "  2. turn ON  'Disable registration'     (this is what closes the door)"
echo "Then run verify.sh."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
HOST="${1:?usage: verify.sh <2fauth-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud>}"
body=$(mktemp)

# (1) require 200. redu's proxy answers 502 for the first couple of minutes while the container
# starts, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" assertion below.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/up")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run in a minute."
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /up answered $code, not 200. Nothing below can be trusted."
  exit 3
fi

# (2) require something app-specific. healthcheck.css is 2FAuth's own and, unlike the heading,
# does not change when APP_NAME does.
if ! grep -q 'healthcheck.css' "$body"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /up answered 200 but the body is not 2FAuth's health page."
  exit 3
fi
echo "OK: talking to 2FAuth"

# (3) positive control for step 4: the landing page really does carry the settings blob, so an
# assertion about its contents can mean something. Without this, a changed template reads as a pass.
land=$(mktemp)
curl -sS -o "$land" "https://$HOST/"
if ! grep -q 'var appSettings = {' "$land"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the landing page has no appSettings block. The template moved; check by hand."
  exit 3
fi
echo "OK: settings block present"

# (4) the assertion. This flag is on the enforcement path: RegisterController returns 403 when it
# is true, for the first account as well as later ones.
if ! grep -q '"disableRegistration":true' "$land"; then
  echo "FAIL: registration is still OPEN. Anyone can create an account on this instance."
  echo "      If nobody has registered yet, the NEXT visitor becomes the administrator."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: registration is closed"
echo
echo "Still to check by hand, because no anonymous request can see it: that 'Protect sensitive"
echo "data' is ON in Settings. The seeds are stored in clear text until it is."

---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/Bubka/2FAuth
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: 2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1
  port: 8000
  vm: m1.small
  flavor_id: "2"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0348
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: 2fauth
quirks:
  - "PIN 2fauth/2fauth:8.0.1, AND NOTE THE TAG STRING DIFFERS FROM THE RELEASE. Docker Hub publishes 8.0.1, 8.0, 8 and a rolling tag; the GitHub release for the same build is v8.0.1, with a leading v. Copying the release name into the compose gives you a pull failure that reads like a network problem. Confirmed against the Docker Hub tag list on 2026-08-17. Never use a rolling tag for a credential store: the entrypoint migrates the schema when the image's commit differs from the marker file, so an unpinned redeploy migrates the vault whenever upstream ships."
  - "⛔⛔ WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: THE FIRST PERSON TO SUBMIT THE SIGN-UP FORM, AND THERE IS NO WAY TO CLOSE THAT AT DEPLOY TIME. app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.php promotes the new account to administrator when User::count() == 1, and registration is open because config/2fauth.php seeds disableRegistration = false. That setting lives in the database, not the environment, so there is no variable you can pass to deploy_compose that closes the window. It closes when YOU register. Do it as the first action after the container answers, before the URL goes anywhere, then turn Disable registration ON in Settings, then run the verification script in this file. Never hand over a 2FAuth URL that nobody has claimed: the person who claims it can read every code you later store."
  - "⛔⛔ TURN ON \"Protect sensitive data\" OR THE SEEDS SIT IN THE DATABASE IN PLAIN TEXT. config/2fauth.php sets useEncryption = false by default, and app/Models/Traits/CanEncryptField.php only reaches for Laravel's Crypt when that setting is true. Everything else about the deploy can be perfect and the twofaccounts table will still hold every TOTP seed, account name and service name in the clear, readable by anyone who reaches the managed database or a backup of it. Turn it on in the admin settings immediately after you claim the account and BEFORE importing anything real."
  - "⛔⛔ APP_KEY IS THE SHARPEST SECRET IN THIS WHOLE LIBRARY, AND IT FAILS QUIETLY. Once encryption is on, APP_KEY decrypts every stored seed. Generate one 32-byte value, keep it, and pass the SAME value on every redeploy. Get it wrong and nothing errors: CanEncryptField::decryptOrReturn catches the exception and returns the translated 'indecipherable' placeholder, so you get a healthy app, a full-looking list of accounts, and not one working code. Losing this key destroys every two-factor account in the vault, which is worse than losing the database, because the user may no longer be able to sign in to the services those codes protect. If you ever must rotate it, put the OLD value in APP_PREVIOUS_KEYS first (.env.example:38-45 documents exactly this) and let the app re-encrypt. ⚠️ An empty APP_KEY does not stop the container either: docker/entrypoint.sh prints a warning line and carries on."
  - "⛔⛔ THE /2fauth VOLUME IS NOT OPTIONAL AND LOSING IT WIPES THE MANAGED DATABASE. This is the trap that a managed database makes WORSE rather than better. docker/entrypoint.sh checks for the marker file /2fauth/installed: if it is missing it runs php artisan migrate:fresh --force, which DROPS EVERY TABLE and recreates them empty. The marker lives on the app VM's volume; the accounts live in the managed Postgres. So a fresh app VM pointed at an existing 2FAuth database boots, sees no marker, drops the vault, and comes up perfectly healthy and completely empty. Mount a volume on /2fauth and keep it. If the volume is ever lost, DO NOT boot the image against the surviving database until you have restored it; the marker alone is not enough, because /2fauth also holds the Passport keys and the storage tree. The real backup is the account export from the 2FAuth UI, and it is worth taking before any redeploy."
  - "USE A NAMED DOCKER VOLUME FOR /2fauth, NOT A BIND MOUNT. The Dockerfile runs the app as UID 1000 and creates /2fauth chmod 700 owned by 1000:1000. A bind mount from a host directory arrives owned by root and the container, which has no root, cannot write to it; upstream's own compose uses ./2fauth and quietly assumes you fixed that. A named volume inherits the image's ownership on first use and just works."
  - "⛔ DATABASE: THE IMAGE SHIPS WITH SQLITE ALREADY CHOSEN. This is not a variable you forget, it is a default you must actively override: the Dockerfile bakes DB_CONNECTION=sqlite and DB_DATABASE=/srv/database/database.sqlite into the image, and the entrypoint symlinks that path to /2fauth/database.sqlite. Set DB_CONNECTION=pgsql and map redu's injected variables yourself, because deploy_compose only appends them to the project .env and never edits your compose: DB_HOST=\"${PGHOST}\", DB_PORT=\"${PGPORT}\", DB_DATABASE=\"${PGDATABASE}\", DB_USERNAME=\"${PGUSER}\", DB_PASSWORD=\"${PGPASSWORD}\". 2FAuth needs exactly ONE database, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule never bites here."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE AN ABSENCE ALONE PROVES NOTHING. Positive half, which is also what tells you the exec worked at all: sudo docker exec <container> printenv DB_CONNECTION DB_HOST must print pgsql and the private IP of the managed database. Negative half: sudo docker exec <container> ls -l /2fauth must show NO database.sqlite. If the first command errors, the second one's empty output means nothing. The VM runs docker, not podman."
  - "SET APP_URL TO THE FULL https HOSTNAME OR WEBAUTHN NEVER WORKS. .env.example is explicit: the variable must match the installation's external address or WebAuthn breaks, because the browser binds a passkey to the origin. Since it has to be known before the container starts, GENERATE THE dname YOURSELF in the full 2fauth-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form and pass it as APP_URL; a bare label gets a random suffix appended by redu and will not match. Set TRUSTED_PROXIES=* at the same time (it defaults to null), because redu terminates TLS at its proxy and 2FAuth otherwise records the proxy's address for every login and can misjudge whether the request was secure."
  - "PORT 8000, and the health anchor is GET /up. The Dockerfile exposes 8000/tcp and nginx listens there. routes/web.php strips session, CSRF, binding and language middleware off /up, so it answers before anything else is ready, and its body links healthcheck.css, which is a 2FAuth-specific string that does not depend on APP_NAME. Pass 8000 to deploy_compose. There is no HEALTHCHECK in the image."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST CAN REACH, ANSWERED PLAINLY. GET /up; GET /manifest.json; GET /api/v1/user/name, a deprecated stub that returns {'deprecation': true} and nothing else; and the landing page, whose inline script carries the real values of disableRegistration, enableSso and useSsoOnly while every other setting is deliberately nulled (SinglePageController.php). No account data, no seeds and no user list are reachable without authentication. The one thing an anonymous visitor CAN do on a fresh instance is claim the administrator account, which is the quirk above."
  - "THE ADMIN PASSWORD IS THE ONLY WAY BACK IN BY DEFAULT. Mail is unconfigured out of the box, so the 'lost password' e-mail goes nowhere, and the recovery paths that exist (password reset by e-mail, WebAuthn device recovery) both need working SMTP. Hand the password to the user in the session and tell them to store it somewhere that is NOT this instance. ⚠️ There is a real circularity here worth saying out loud: this app holds the second factor for their other accounts, so locking themselves out of it is expensive. Configure MAIL_* and SITE_OWNER if they want recovery, or add a passkey once they are signed in."
  - "USE UPSTREAM'S COMPOSE AS A SHAPE, NOT A FILE. docker/docker-compose.yml is four useful lines: one service, the image, a volume at /2fauth and port 8000. Drop the obsolete version key, drop the env_file indirection that points at settings.env, and write the environment inline so the PG* interpolation is visible, and use a named volume as described above. There are no bundled databases, proxies or sidecars to delete, which is why this is one of the cheapest entries here."
  - "NO migrate_command NEEDED, AND DO NOT ADD ONE. docker/entrypoint.sh runs the migrations itself, chooses between migrate and migrate:fresh on the marker file, runs passport:install on a genuinely fresh install, then optimizes and starts supervisord. Adding your own migrate step can only interfere with that decision. QUEUE_DRIVER is sync and CACHE_DRIVER and SESSION_DRIVER are file, so no Redis is needed; sessions land in /2fauth/storage and survive a container restart."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO FIGURE. It is an alpine image running nginx and php-fpm for one small Laravel app, so m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) is a reasonable floor and makes this one of the cheapest entries in the library. The one thing that spikes is QR-code decoding: .env.example documents PHP_MEMORY_LIMIT_TEMP_OVERRIDE=512, a temporary 512 MB per-request limit applied so image scanning does not exhaust memory. That fits inside 2 GB for a personal vault; move to m1.medium if a team will be importing at once. Measure it on your run and write the number back rather than repeating this paragraph."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.035/hr, roughly GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id '2' (m1.small), database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2', port 8000. ⚠️ plan_deploy will want to upsize a compose stack to m1.large; passing flavor_id '2' explicitly holds m1.small, and the larger floor exists for stacks that BUILD from source, which this does not. Always pass db_flavor_id explicitly or the database VM inherits the app flavor and doubles the bill."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built. Write the one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar and curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo."
  - "LICENCE: AGPL-3.0, read from the LICENSE file, and this one has a clause worth a sentence. Section 13 says that if you MODIFY the program and let other people use it over a network, you must offer those users the modified source. Running the published image unmodified for yourself or your team creates no such obligation. It falls on whoever OPERATES the service, which here is the user, not redu, and it is one more reason to deploy the pinned upstream image rather than a fork."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. APP_KEY, the admin password and the database password all belong to the user. Hand them over in the session; the deploy log records that an admin exists, that registration is closed and that encryption is on, never the values. Generate the password alphanumeric so there is nothing to escape in JSON or the shell."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back. ⚠️ The merge does NOT write new quirks: when this file is richer than redu's template it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Anything the run teaches has to be added by hand."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, AND THAT COMBINATION IS DANGEROUS HERE. delete_deployment removes the app VM and the /2fauth volume with it, while the managed Postgres keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr with every account still in it. Redeploying onto that surviving database with no volume is exactly the migrate:fresh wipe described above. So either delete the database too with delete_database, or restore the volume before the next boot. Say which, plainly, before deleting anything."

# Self-host 2FAuth on redu

Your two-factor codes on your own machine: one small container, a managed Postgres, a public HTTPS
URL. About GBP 25 a month, inside the no-card free trial, and one of the cheapest entries here.

## What this deploys

- **2FAuth** from the official Docker Hub image, pinned to `8.0.1`, on one m1.small VM, port 8000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding the accounts.
- A named volume on `/2fauth`, which holds the storage tree, the Passport keys and the install
  marker. Read the warning below before you treat it as disposable.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy 2FAuth on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## Three things, and all three lose data

**Claim the account immediately.** The first person to submit the sign-up form becomes the
administrator, and there is no environment variable that closes that window before the hostname is
live. The setting that disables registration lives in the database and can only be set from inside
the app. So the window closes when you register, and not a moment earlier.

**Turn on encryption before you store anything.** 2FAuth ships with `useEncryption` off, which
means the seeds sit in the database in plain text. Turn on "Protect sensitive data" in the admin
settings first, then import.

**Keep `APP_KEY` and keep the `/2fauth` volume.** The key decrypts every seed, and a wrong one
does not error: the app shows a full list of accounts and not one working code. The volume holds
the install marker, and without it the container drops every table in your managed database and
comes up healthy and empty.

## Claim the administrator account

Run this the moment the container answers. Generate the password alphanumeric, at least eight
characters, and never write it into this file.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
HOST="${1:?usage: claim.sh <2fauth-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud>}"
: "${ADMIN_NAME:?set ADMIN_NAME}"
: "${ADMIN_EMAIL:?set ADMIN_EMAIL}"
: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD:[REDACTED:value] ADMIN_PASSWORD, at least 8 characters}"

JAR=$(mktemp)
OUT=$(mktemp)

# The registration endpoint is a session route, so it needs a CSRF token from the same session.
TOKEN=«REDACTED:assigned:ce5757dd» -sS -c "$JAR" "https://$HOST/refresh-csrf")
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: no CSRF token returned, the app is probably still starting. Re-run."
  exit 3
fi

# printf is a shell builtin, so the password never appears in ps, and the body goes on stdin.
code=$(printf '{"name":"%s","email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]","password_confirmation":"[REDACTED:value]"}' \
  "$ADMIN_NAME" "$ADMIN_EMAIL" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" "$ADMIN_PASSWORD" |
  curl -sS -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" -X POST "https://$HOST/user" \
    -H "X-CSRF-TOKEN: [REDACTED:value]" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'Accept: application/json' \
    --data-binary @- -o "$OUT" -w '%{http_code}')

if [ "$code" != "201" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: registration answered $code, not 201. Body:"
  cat "$OUT"
  echo
  echo "Register in a browser NOW instead, and do not leave this instance unclaimed."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: administrator account created. Now sign in and, in Settings:"
echo "  1. turn ON  'Protect sensitive data'   (this is what encrypts the seeds)"
echo "  2. turn ON  'Disable registration'     (this is what closes the door)"
echo "Then run verify.sh."
```

## Then prove it, from outside

This refuses to guess. It establishes that it is talking to 2FAuth before it believes anything, and
exits 3 rather than passing when it cannot tell.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
HOST="${1:?usage: verify.sh <2fauth-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud>}"
body=$(mktemp)

# (1) require 200. redu's proxy answers 502 for the first couple of minutes while the container
# starts, and an error page fails every "did it NOT do X" assertion below.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/up")
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the proxy, the container is still starting. Re-run in a minute."
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /up answered $code, not 200. Nothing below can be trusted."
  exit 3
fi

# (2) require something app-specific. healthcheck.css is 2FAuth's own and, unlike the heading,
# does not change when APP_NAME does.
if ! grep -q 'healthcheck.css' "$body"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /up answered 200 but the body is not 2FAuth's health page."
  exit 3
fi
echo "OK: talking to 2FAuth"

# (3) positive control for step 4: the landing page really does carry the settings blob, so an
# assertion about its contents can mean something. Without this, a changed template reads as a pass.
land=$(mktemp)
curl -sS -o "$land" "https://$HOST/"
if ! grep -q 'var appSettings = {' "$land"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: the landing page has no appSettings block. The template moved; check by hand."
  exit 3
fi
echo "OK: settings block present"

# (4) the assertion. This flag is on the enforcement path: RegisterController returns 403 when it
# is true, for the first account as well as later ones.
if ! grep -q '"disableRegistration":true' "$land"; then
  echo "FAIL: registration is still OPEN. Anyone can create an account on this instance."
  echo "      If nobody has registered yet, the NEXT visitor becomes the administrator."
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: registration is closed"
echo
echo "Still to check by hand, because no anonymous request can see it: that 'Protect sensitive"
echo "data' is ON in Settings. The seeds are stored in clear text until it is."
```
